### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for best results. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Gather Components** | • CPU (Intel/AMD)
• Motherboard (socket, chipset, form‑factor)
• RAM (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity)
• GPU (if not integrated)
• Storage (SSD/HDD, NVMe or SATA)
• Power Supply Unit (PSU, wattage, 80+ rating)
• Case (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX, size, airflow)
• Cooling (stock cooler, aftermarket air cooler, AIO liquid cooler)
• Operating System (Windows, Linux, etc.) | Check the motherboard’s CPU socket and RAM type. Verify PSU wattage with a PSU calculator. | | 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | • Clean, flat, static‑free surface.
• Anti‑static wrist strap (recommended).
• Screwdrivers (Phillips #0, #1). | Keep all screws in a small container or magnetic tray. | | 4 | **Install the CPU** | 1. Open the CPU socket latch.
2. Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket corner.
3. Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide. | | 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount on the CPU.
• Mount the cooler according to its instructions. | For AIO coolers, attach the pump to the motherboard header. | | 6 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch on the RAM stick with the slot key.
• Push firmly until the clips click. | Install in the recommended slots (often 1 & 3 for dual‑channel). | | 7 | **Mount the Motherboard** | 1. Place standoffs in the case (matching motherboard size).
2. Align the motherboard with the I/O shield and standoffs.
3. Secure with screws. | Double‑check that all screw holes line up. | | 8 | **Install Storage** | • For NVMe SSDs: slide into the M.2 slot, screw down.
• For SATA SSD/HDD: mount in drive bay, connect SATA data & power cables. | Label cables if you have many. | | 9 | **Install GPU** | 1. Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers on the case.
2. Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
3. Secure with screws. | Connect any required PCI‑e power connectors from the PSU. | | 10 | **Connect Power** | • PSU to motherboard (24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS).
• CPU power (4/8‑pin).
• GPU power (6/8‑pin).
• Storage & case fans. | Keep cables tidy; use cable ties or Velcro straps. | | 11 | **Connect Front Panel & USB** | • Refer to the motherboard manual for pin layout.
• Connect power button, reset button, USB headers, audio jacks. | Double‑check orientation; reversed connections can damage components. | | 12 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables behind the motherboard tray.
• Use cable ties to bundle. | Good airflow = better cooling. | | 13 | **First Boot** | 1. Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
2. Power on.
3. Enter BIOS/UEFI (usually F2, Del, Esc). | Check that all components are recognized (CPU, RAM, GPU, storage). | | 14 | **Update BIOS/UEFI** | • Download latest firmware from motherboard manufacturer.
• Flash via BIOS update utility. | Follow the manufacturer’s instructions carefully. | | 15 | **Install Operating System** | • Create bootable USB (Windows Media Creation Tool, Rufus, or Linux ISO).
• Boot from USB, install OS. | Install drivers after OS installation (chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi). | | 16 | **Install Drivers & Software** | • GPU drivers (NVIDIA GeForce Experience, AMD Radeon Software).
• Motherboard chipset drivers.
• Peripheral drivers. | Keep your system updated for stability and performance. | | 17 | **Test & Benchmark** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | Ensure temperatures stay within safe limits. | | 18 | **Final Tweaks** | • Adjust fan curves.
• Enable XMP profile for RAM.
• Set boot priority. | Save BIOS settings. | | 19 | **Enjoy!** | • Install games, software, or start your workflow. | Keep your system clean and updated. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU socket & cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated correctly - [ ] Motherboard mounted on standoffs - [ ] PSU connected to motherboard, CPU, GPU - [ ] GPU seated and powered - [ ] Storage installed and connected - [ ] Front panel connectors attached - [ ] Cables managed and secured - [ ] BIOS updated - [ ] OS installed - [ ] Drivers installed - [ ] System tested --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | PC won’t power on | PSU not connected or switched off | Check PSU switch, verify all power cables | | GPU not detected | Wrong PCI‑e slot or missing power connector | Move GPU to top slot, connect power | | Overheating | Poor airflow, insufficient cooling | Re‑route cables, add case fans, re‑apply thermal paste | | BIOS not recognizing RAM | Incorrect slot or incompatible RAM | Install in correct slots, check compatibility | | Blue screen on boot | Driver conflict or faulty component | Update drivers, run memory test (MemTest86) | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – component compatibility checker - **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* - **Manufacturer Manuals** – always keep a PDF handy - **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
